Article Title: GST collections cross Rs 2 lakh crore again, rise 14.7% in September
Article Text:
GST collections cross Rs 2 lakh crore

India’s gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections once again crossed the Rs 2 lakh crore mark in September, rising 14.7% year-on-year to Rs 2.04 lakh crore, according to government data. The increase was driven by higher revenue from both domestic transactions and imports.Revenue from domestic transactions grew 10.1% to Rs 1.38 lakh crore in September 2026, compared with Rs 1.25 lakh crore in the corresponding month last year. GST revenue from imports, meanwhile, rose 25.9% year-on-year to Rs 65,525 crore from Rs 52,031 crore.Gross Integrated GST (IGST) collections increased to Rs 1.20 lakh crore during the month, against Rs 1.02 lakh crore in September 2025. Central GST collections stood at Rs 37,762 crore, while State GST collections were at Rs 45,363 crore.The rise in gross collections came even as GST refunds declined during the month. Total refunds stood at Rs 27,001 crore in September, down 3% from Rs 27,848 crore a year earlier.According to Abhishek Jain, indirect tax head & partner at KPMG, the growth in GST collections is encouraging, but the sharp rise in import GST needs to be examined further.“Gross GST collections growing 14.7% in September despite global headwinds is very encouraging. As import GST is up nearly 26%; it's important to see how much of that is raw materials versus finished goods.”Jain further added, “It’ll be good to analyse this in detail, specifically if it signals already stronger domestic manufacturing or there is a need for further push, thereby making stronger the case for continuing and expanding schemes like PLI.”Domestic refunds fell 13.5% year-on-year to Rs 13,504 crore. In contrast, export GST refunds processed through ICEGATE rose 10.2% to Rs 13,497 crore.With refunds taken into account, net GST collections grew faster than gross collections. Net revenue rose 18.1% year-on-year to Rs 1.77 lakh crore in September, compared with Rs 1.50 lakh crore in September 2025.Net domestic GST revenue increased 13.5% to Rs 1.24 lakh crore, while net revenue from customs-related GST jumped 30.8% to Rs 52,028 crore.The September figures also pushed up the GST collection tally for the first six months of the financial year. Between April and September, gross GST collections rose 11.6% to Rs 12.46 lakh crore, compared with Rs 11.17 lakh crore in the same period of 2025-26.Net GST collections during the April-September period increased 10.4% to Rs 10.66 lakh crore from Rs 9.65 lakh crore a year earlier.In terms of states, Maharashtra emerged as the largest contributor among the states listed, recording GST revenue of Rs 29,986 crore in September, a 15% year-on-year increase. Karnataka's collections rose 16% to Rs 13,884 crore, while Gujarat recorded Rs 12,222 crore, up 17%.Uttar Pradesh and Telangana both registered 18% growth in GST revenue during the month. Uttar Pradesh collected Rs 8,882 crore, while Telangana recorded Rs 5,327 crore.
Article Summary: Gross Goods and Services Tax collections rose 14.7% year-on-year to Rs 2.04 lakh crore in September. The increase was driven by higher revenue from both domestic transactions and imports. The rise in gross collections came even as GST refunds declined during the month.

Article Title: Why stock market was down today? Rs 6 lakh crore wiped out; Sensex, Nifty suffer worst losing streak in 25 years
Article Text:
Bloodbath at Dalal Street

FII selling intensifies

US bond yields hit multi-year highs

Rupee remains under pressure

Crude close to $100

Auto and infra stocks drag D-Street

Nifty’s key psychological levels breached

NEW DELHI: Dalal Street suffered its worst and longest losing streak in nearly 25 years, with investors losing over Rs 6 lakh crore. Benchmark indices came under heavy selling pressure on Thursday, with BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty50 falling more than 1% as persistent foreign investor outflows, rising US bond yields and pressure on rupee weighed down sentiments.During the session, the BSE Sensex plunged more than 1,000 points to fall below the 71,600 mark, while the NSE Nifty50 dropped over 300 points to slip below 22,300. The indices, however, pared some of their losses later in the session. Sensex eventually closed 570.59 points, or 0.79%, lower at 71,909.70, while Nifty50 fell 205.40 points, or 0.91%, to settle at 22,282.75.This brutal selloff the dragged total market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE to Rs 466 lakh crore.With markets set to remain closed on Friday, investors turned cautious ahead of the extended break. Here are the key factors behind Thursday’s selloff on Dalal Street:Foreign investors remained a major source of pressure on Indian equities, turning net sellers across all reported equity and debt segments in September for the first time in two years. They sold Indian equities worth $1.06 billion on Wednesday, while exchange data showed FII selling of Rs 10,148.41 crore on the same day.Their selling over the previous five sessions stood at about $3.6 billion, taking their year-to-date selling to a record $27.8 billion."The sustained FII selling became intense during the last two trading days when the FIIs sold equity for a total of Rs 20,128 crore. With the US 10-year bond yield rising further to 5.3 per cent, FIIs may continue to sell. An apparent contradiction in the FII activity is that even while selling through the exchanges, they have been consistently investing through the primary market and also buying expensive mid and smallcaps," V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist, Geojit Investments Limited, said.FPIs had been net buyers in equities in July and August, with purchases of Rs 20,200 crore and Rs 29,631 crore, respectively. However, they were net sellers of Rs 35,861 crore in stocks till September 29. After another Rs 10,148 crore of selling on September 30, the month's total stock selling stood at about Rs 46,000 crore, according to NSDL and BSE data.For the current year, FPI net selling in equities has reached Rs 2.6 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.7 lakh crore in the previous year. The 2026 outflow is now the highest-ever annual net selling figure, NSDL data showed.Rising US treasury yields added to the pressure on equities. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.31%, its highest level since 2007. It rose more than 87 basis points during the September quarter, marking its biggest quarterly increase since 1994, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters.The 30-year Treasury yield also moved above 5.65%, reaching its highest level since 2002.Higher bond yields can make debt markets more attractive to investors, putting pressure on riskier equity markets. Bond yields move inversely to bond prices, so the sharp rise in yields reflected an intense selloff in bonds."The domestic market remains under pressure after extending its decline, with September marking the Nifty's steepest monthly fall since March. Foreign selling and elevated global borrowing costs continue to weigh on sentiment, although the easing in crude prices and softer US inflation provide some counterweight," Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder & CEO of HST Wealth, a research analyst firm, said.Rupee fell 0.16% to 95.9850 per dollar as the dollar index rose to a more than three-month high amid higher US Treasury yields. Losses were limited as state-run banks sold dollars, likely on behalf of the RBI, Reuters reported.Anil Bhansali, head of advisory at Finrex Treasury Advisors, said that the 96 against the greenback is a crucial level."The 96 level remains an important psychological and technical area, with the rupee showing some resilience each time it approaches that level, thanks largely due to the Reserve Bank of India."In afternoon trade, Brent crude inched 1.87% high to trade around $99.86 per barrel, while WTI crude gained 2.01% to $92.24 per barrel. Brent crude futures have continued to remain near $97 a barrel after Tehran said it had received Washington's response to its latest ceasefire proposal.Crude oil prices remain a critical bellwether for the equity markets. Because India imports over 85% of its crude oil requirements, fluctuations in global energy prices directly ripple through the country's macroeconomic fundamentals.The selloff was broad-based, with several heavyweight stocks coming under pressure. Among the 30 Sensex companies, Mahindra & Mahindra, Maruti, UltraTech Cement, Bharat Electronics, Eternal and Asian Paints were among the major laggards.Maruti fell 4.93%, M&M 4.24%, Tata Steel 4.20%, Adani Ports 3.47%, ITC 3.20%, UltraTech Cement 3.01%, Power Grid 2.76% and Eternal 2.75%.Other major losers included HUL, BEL, Trent, NTPC, Larsen & Toubro, Bajaj Finance, Reliance Industries, Titan, IndiGo and Bharti Airtel.In contrast, Infosys, HDFC Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and HCL Tech were among the stocks showing gains during the session. Axis Bank, TCS and ICICI Bank were also among the stocks in the green or near-flat zone.US markets ended mostly lower on Wednesday, adding to the cautious mood in domestic equities.The market decline was also exacerbated after the benchmark indices broke through key technical levels.The Nifty had closed at 22,620 on Wednesday. Hemang Gor, senior research analyst of derivatives and technical research, as cited by ET, identified 22,500 as the index's first support level and warned that a break below it could expose the benchmark to a fall towards 22,400.The Nifty subsequently moved below the second support level as well.Axis Securities had also identified 22,500 as the first support level and said a break below it could drag the index towards 22,300. “Conversely, a sustained move above 22,800 could strengthen the upward momentum, opening the door for a move toward the 23,000–23,100 zone,” said Axis Securities.Meanwhile, "With markets to be closed tomorrow, the session is seeing cautious positioning ahead of the extended break," said Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder and CEO of HST Wealth.
Article Summary: BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty50 fall more than 1% as persistent foreign investor outflows, rising US bond yields and pressure on rupee weighed down sentiments. FPI net selling in equities has reached Rs 2.6 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.7 lakh crore last year.

Article Title: Unscrupulous jewellers may use fake stamps to mark your gold: As hallmarking charges rise to Rs 75 from Rs 45 Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council flags risk of rise in fraudsters
Article Text:
BIS hallmarking serves as a system for determining the purity of precious metal articles. (Image for representative purpose only)

Gold hallmarking

Process of hallmarking

Gold hallmarking, a sign that allows you to verify the purity of the gold you are purchasing, has become costlier. And, the fallout of that is that there is a possible rise in fraudsters who are selling gold with fake stamps.The increase in gold hallmarking charges has raised concerns within the industry that the higher cost could encourage unscrupulous jewellers to resort to counterfeit hallmarking stamps.The concern is being considered particularly relevant in tier-2, tier-3 and tier-4 cities, where consumer awareness remains limited.Consumers bear the hallmarking cost when purchasing jewellery. However, many buyers are still unaware that they can verify the Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number through the Bureau of Indian Standards' Care mobile application.Rajesh Rokde, chairman of the All-India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC), told ET that awareness of the BIS app is adequate in only around 10% of the country’s 800 districts.This, he said, leaves consumers exposed as fraudsters develop increasingly sophisticated methods of copying hallmarking safeguards, including photographs.The GJC has taken up the matter with consumer affairs minister Pralhad Joshi and the BIS, asking that the earlier rate of Rs 45 per article be restored from the current Rs 75.The latest increase is a 66.67% hike, which the council said has added considerably to the compliance burden under a system that is mandatory.The industry body has also raised questions over whether the higher fee has resulted in a comparable improvement in consumer protection.Data from the government cited by the GJC shows that the number of recognised assaying and hallmarking centres (AHCs) rose to 1,577 in July 2026 from 1,220 in July 2022. During the same period, the cumulative number of gold articles hallmarked with HUID crossed 650 million.Hallmarking activity has grown significantly as well. A total of 132.2 million jewellery articles were hallmarked in 2025-26. Based on the revised fee, the GJC estimates that the additional financial burden on the ecosystem could be around Rs 400 crore, apart from approximately Rs 80 crore in GST.The GJC has asked the BIS to provide a detailed assessment of the costs underlying the revised charge, including expenditure on additional equipment, manpower, processing and storage. The council has also questioned the additional expense linked to mandatory photography, pointing out that photographs could potentially be copied or manipulated by fraudsters.According to the council, the turnaround time for hallmarking has also lengthened considerably, rising from around six hours earlier to 24-36 hours. This is resulting in jewellers' working capital being tied up for longer periods and adding to their financing costs.The hallmarking fee for silver articles has not been changed and continues to be Rs 35.The revised rates were notified through the BIS (Hallmarking) Amendment Regulations, 2026, dated September 14, 2026.BIS hallmarking serves as a system for determining the purity of precious metal articles and certifying them under the Bureau of Indian Standards framework. A hallmarked article carries three important identifiers: the BIS logo, the karat or millesimal fineness and a six-digit alphanumeric Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number.Jewellers seeking to sell hallmarked jewellery are required to register with the Bureau of Indian Standards first. The registration process is entirely online. The jeweller files an application through the BIS portal, following which the registration is issued instantly and can be downloaded. No registration fee is charged, and once granted, the registration remains valid for the jeweller's lifetime.After obtaining registration, the jeweller sends the jewellery to a BIS-recognised Assaying & Hallmarking (A&H) Centre for examination. The centre tests the articles to establish whether they conform to the prescribed standards. When an article clears the required tests, the A&H Centre applies the hallmark to the jewellery.
Article Summary: The increase in gold hallmarking charges has raised concerns within the industry that the higher cost could encourage unscrupulous jewellers to resort to counterfeit hallmarking stamps. Consumers bear the hallmarking cost when purchasing jewellery. Many buyers are still unaware that they can verify the Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number through the Bureau of Indian Standards' Care mobile application.

Article Title: No long leave needed: Why short, mindful getaways are having a moment
Article Text:
Short getaways are finding favour

Short, mindful getaways are getting popular

No long leave needed to feel refreshed

Disclaimer: The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.

Between back-to-back meetings, packed calendars and the constant ping of notifications, taking a proper holiday can sometimes feel like another task on the to-do list. That is perhaps why short getaways are finding favour with travellers who want to step away from the daily grind without taking too much time off.From extending a work trip by a couple of days to turning a quick road trip into a wellness break, bleisure is taking on a more relaxed meaning. The idea is simple: work when you need to, and make the most of the time when you don't. For many urban travellers, a good hotel now needs to offer both, a comfortable space to catch up on work and enough reasons to put the laptop away.Radisson Hotel Group’s portfolio has several stays that fit this new way of travelling. Radisson Resort & Spa Khopoli, a drive away from Mumbai and Pune, offers the kind of nature-filled setting where a workday can give way to a spa session, yoga or some pool time. At Radisson Hotel Nathdwara, travellers can combine a spiritual escape with wellness experiences at the R3 Spa, yoga room, rooftop pool and fitness centre.For those who would rather trade city noise for mountain air, Radisson Resort Hatgad Saputara offers a relaxed hill escape with yoga, spa and leisure experiences, while Radisson Hotel Kufri brings the appeal of a quieter Himalayan break. Radisson Blu Palace Resort & Spa, Udaipur adds a touch of luxury to the mix, allowing travellers to combine wellness, culture and leisure in one short stay.Because sometimes, you don't need a week-long holiday to feel refreshed. You just need a change of view, a little less screen time and a couple of days that are entirely your own.
Article Summary: Short getaways are finding favour with travellers who want to step away from the daily grind without taking too much time off. The idea is simple: work when you need to, and make the most of the time when you don't. For many urban travellers, a good hotel now needs to offer both a comfortable space to catch up on work and enough reasons to put the laptop away.

Article Title: Consumer loans, credit card dues enter slow lane
Article Text:
AI-generated image

MUMBAI: Consumer demand appears to be losing momentum, with loans for consumer durables and credit card outstandings growing just 2.4% and 3.6% year on year, respectively, in Aug. At the same time, banks have seen strong demand for secured borrowing, with gold loans adding Rs 98,096 crore in the first five months of FY27, almost matching the Rs 98,858 crore added through home loans.According to RBI sectoral credit data, bank credit rose by about Rs 10.3 lakh crore, or 4.8%, between April and Aug 2026, taking outstanding credit to Rs 223.9 lakh crore. While overall credit grew 19.1% year- on-year, the composition of incremental lending during the first five months of FY27 shows weaker growth in discretionary consumer credit and stronger demand for secured retail loans, corporate credit and lending to NBFCs.Credit card outstandings rose to about Rs 3 lakh crore in Aug but added only Rs 4,740 crore during the first five months of FY27. Consumer durable loans stood at Rs 23,295 crore, adding just Rs 1,333 crore during the period. Vehicle loans remained stronger, growing 19.7% year on year to Rs 7.8 lakh crore and adding Rs 37,027 crore between April and Aug.Gold loans were a major source of retail credit growth. Outstanding loans against gold jewellery rose 83.2% year-on-year to Rs 5.6 lakh crore in Aug from about Rs 3 lakh crore a year earlier.The Rs 98,096 crore increase in gold loans accounted for 9.6% of incremental bank credit during the five months, almost matching the 9.6% share of home loans. Advances against fixed deposits also rose 43.2% year on year to Rs 2 lakh crore, adding Rs 35,166 crore during the period.The broader personal loan category added Rs 3.5 lakh crore, accounting for 33.9% of incremental bank credit. Outstanding retail credit stood at Rs 72.9 lakh crore in Aug, up 16.9% year-on-year. Services accounted for Rs 2.4 lakh crore, or 23%, of incremental credit. Bank lending to NBFCs rose 37.5% year-on-year to Rs 21.6 lakh crore, with their borrowings from banks increasing by Rs 93,870 crore. Lending to public financial institutions rose 83.7%.
Article Summary: Bank credit rose by about Rs 10.3 lakh crore, or 4.8%, between April and Aug 2026. Outstanding retail credit stood at Rs 72.9 lakh crore in Aug, up 16.9% year-on-year. Gold loans accounted for 9.6% of incremental bank credit during the five months.

Article Title: Indian oil refiners change strategy to get cheaper oil; hire ships & tankers to sail through Strait of Hormuz
Article Text:
The shift in approach follows a recovery in oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz in recent months.

Why Indian oil refiners have changed strategy

Amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict, India’s oil refiners are changing tactics to procure crude from the Middle East through the Strait of Hormuz. This narrow channel of water has been effectively shut since the start of the war in March, with limited ships and tankers passing through.Indian oil refiners are now chartering tankers to travel through the Strait of Hormuz and collect crude from inside the Persian Gulf. This marks a notable change in their approach as they seek to lower costs and strengthen the reliability of their supply chains.The strategy is a departure from the approach Indian refiners have followed since the early stages of the US-Iran war. Concerned about the possibility of attacks, refiners had refrained from sending their own vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.Also Read | Trade irony amid Trump threat: Why Russia is buying its own oil as fuel from India Instead, they left the risks associated with navigating the disputed waterway to Gulf producers and international trading companies, which transported the crude to India. This arrangement came at a significant additional cost, with refiners paying a substantial premium under so-called cost and freight terms.That approach has started to change in recent weeks, according to a Bloomberg report. Indian Oil Corporation, Reliance Industries Ltd.,Bharat Petroleum Corp. and HPCL-Mittal Energy Ltd. have purchased Iraqi crude on a free-on-board basis.Under FOB transactions, the buyer is responsible for arranging the vessel, loading the crude and transporting the cargo to its destination. By opting for such deals, Indian refiners can exercise greater control over transportation costs, although sourcing and locking in suitable tankers remains a challenge.People familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that the refiners have now floated tenders and are in discussions with shipping companies.Sinokor Group and Dynacom Tankers Management Ltd. have so far won tenders, the people said. Shipping Corp. of India and Lila Global had also submitted bids, but the tenders were subsequently cancelled, according to the people quoted in the report.The shift in approach follows a recovery in oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz in recent months, along with the restoration of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline.According to a note issued by JPMorgan Chase & Co. this week, Middle Eastern crude shipments have recovered to 98% of their pre-war levels. At the same time, India is showing greater reluctance to accept Russian cargoes as political pressure from the US increases, the report claimed.Indian refiners had earlier faced difficulties in arranging crude pickups from within the Gulf because New Delhi did not allow vessels undertaking such voyages to use Indian crew.That position changed in August, when the Directorate General of Shipping eased its advisory. Instead of prohibiting Indian seafarers from travelling through Hormuz, the revised guidance asked shipowners and placement agencies to secure the consent of Indian seafarers before they undertook the voyage.The pricing of Iraqi crude could also be a factor behind the refiners’ decision to alter their strategy. SOMO, Iraq’s state-owned oil marketing company, has been offering contracted supplies for October at discounts of as much as $37 a barrel compared with regional benchmarks.Data from Kpler shows that crude volumes travelling through the Strait of Hormuz to India averaged around 1.3 million barrels a day in September.That was the highest level recorded since February, before the war began. Overall, India’s crude imports from the Middle East stand at about 2.8 million barrels a day, including Saudi oil shipped through the Red Sea.
Article Summary: Indian oil refiners are now chartering tankers to travel through the Strait of Hormuz and collect crude from inside the Persian Gulf. This marks a notable change in their approach as they seek to lower costs and strengthen the reliability of their supply chains.

Article Title: UPI daily average transactions continue to rise in September
Article Text:
UPI daily average transactions continue to rise in September

MUMBAI: India’s digital payments activity remained strong in Sept despite lower monthly transaction counts, with daily average UPI value rising to Rs 97,913 crore from Rs 96,205 crore in Aug and IMPS value increasing to Rs 23,530 crore from Rs 22,701 crore, according to National Payments Corporation of India data.Given the lesser number of days in Sept, monthly UPI transaction volume fell to 2,407 crore in Sept from 2,451 crore in Aug, while monthly transaction value declined to Rs 29.37 lakh crore from Rs 29.82 lakh crore. IMPS transactions also fell to 35.4 crore from 36 crore. The declines partly reflected the shorter month, with Sept having 30 days compared with 31 in Aug.On a daily basis, UPI transactions increased to 80.2 crore in Sept from 79.1 crore in Aug. Daily average transaction value rose by Rs 1,708 crore to Rs 97,913 crore. Compared with Sept 2025, daily UPI value increased 18% from around Rs 82,977 crore, while daily transaction volume rose 23% from around 65.2 crore to 80.2 crore.IMPS showed a similar increase in daily value despite the fall in monthly transaction count. Daily average turnover rose 3.65% month-on-month to Rs 23,530 crore in Sept, adding Rs 829 crore to the daily flow compared with Aug.Daily transaction frequency increased to 1.18 crore from 1.16 crore.On a year-on-year basis, daily IMPS transaction value increased 18% from around Rs 19,941 crore in Sep 2025. However, total IMPS transaction volume fell 10%, while UPI transaction volume increased 23%.The contrasting trends point to a shift in the use of the two payment rails. UPI has absorbed a growing share of frequent, lower-value transactions, while IMPS continues to handle larger-value fund transfers. With daily average values rising on both platforms, Sep data points to higher transaction value moving through India’s real-time payments infrastructure despite the lower monthly counts.
Article Summary: India’s digital payments activity remained strong in Sept despite lower monthly transaction counts. Daily average UPI value rising to Rs 97,913 crore from Rs 96,205 crore in Aug. IMPS value increasing to Rs 23,530 crore from £ 22,701 crore, National Payments Corporation of India data shows.

Article Title: 16-year-old boxer trains 75 girls in self-defence through DefendHer initiative
Article Text:
Raval started DefendHer to make self-defence training more accessible to girls from underserved communities

“Self-defence is not just about knowing how to fight,”

“It is about feeling capable enough to respond when something does not feel right, and confident enough to believe that you have a choice.”

Tiara Raval, an IB student, has trained over 75 girls across 26 sessions in Mumbai

“The point is not to turn girls into fighters,”

“It is to make sure they leave knowing that they have skills they can rely on and confidence within themselves,”

.

“Just telling a girl to be confident does not necessarily make her confident,”

“When she begins to trust herself, that confidence becomes more real.”

A self-defence initiative started by 16-year-old student and boxer Tiara Raval, an IB student, has trained over 75 girls across 26 sessions in Mumbai, focusing on practical defence techniques, situational awareness and confidence-building.Raval started DefendHer to make self-defence training more accessible to girls from underserved communities.The programme follows a repeated-session format rather than a one-time self-defence workshop. Participants are introduced to techniques such as jabs, footwork and defence movements, while also working on situational awareness. The format allows girls to return for multiple sessions, practise techniques and become more comfortable applying them over time.Raval began boxing at the age of 12, and her experience with the sport shaped the way she approached DefendHer.she said.She added that boxing taught her discipline and resilience and changed how she thought about confidence and her ability to protect herself. She wanted other girls to experience some of that change through the sessions.During the training, Raval works alongside participants, demonstrating techniques, correcting movements and taking them through drills and exercises. She said one change she has observed is how participants approach the sessions. Girls who were initially hesitant to step forward or unsure about performing a technique gradually became more willing to participate and practise independently.Raval said.she addedTeaching the techniques has also given Raval a different perspective on boxing. Movements that had become instinctive after years of training had to be broken down and explained to girls encountering them for the first time. This required her to adapt sessions according to each participant’s confidence and ability, and to focus not only on demonstrating a movement but on teaching it.Raval believes that practical training can also create space for broader conversations around women’s safety.she said.With approximately 75 girls reached across 26 sessions, Raval plans to continue developing DefendHer while retaining the regular training model that has been central to the initiative. The programme remains focused on giving participants an opportunity to learn, practise and build familiarity with self-defence techniques over time.
Article Summary: Tiara Raval started DefendHer to make self-defence training more accessible to girls from underserved communities. Participants are introduced to techniques such as jabs, footwork and defence movements. The format allows girls to return for multiple sessions, practise techniques and become more comfortable applying them.

Article Title: Scotch whisky gets cheaper in India after UK trade pact: Johnnie Walker Black Label prices falls to Rs 3,800 from Rs 4,250, J&B to Rs 1,700 from Rs 2,300 as tariff drops from 150% to 75%
Article Text:
Before the lower prices could be introduced, the companies were required to submit proposals to state excise authorities.

Scotch whisky prices drop!

State-level pricing differences

Scotch whisky prices in India have dropped by 10-15% for the first time since the India-UK free trade agreement came into force, with Diageo and Pernod Ricard passing on lower import costs to consumers in some key states.In fact, the price cuts for brands such as Johnnie Walker Black Label and J&B have already taken effect in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Goa and Uttar Pradesh, while other states are expected to follow.Under the India-UK agreement, the import tariff on British whisky was reduced to 75% from 150%, effectively cutting the rate by half. The tariff is scheduled to decline further to 40% over the next 10 years. However, the reduction in import duty does not result in a similar reduction in the final retail price, since import duty accounts for only one part of the overall price, along with state excise duties, taxes, distribution expenses and margins.Also Read | Trade irony amid Trump threat: Why Russia is buying its own oil as fuel from India The price reductions mark the first major move by the two largest Scotch producers to adjust consumer prices since the trade agreement became effective on July 15. The cuts are also an early indication of how much of the savings from lower tariffs could eventually be passed on to Indian whisky consumers.Industry sources said Diageo's 750-ml Johnnie Walker Black Label is now available for around Rs 3,800, compared with Rs 4,250 previously.The price of J&B has fallen to about Rs 1,700 from around Rs 2,300 earlier.Pernod Ricard has also approached the government seeking approval for lower prices for brands including Chivas, Ballantine's and The Glenlivet, according to industry executives quoted in an ET report."The UK FTA will have an impact on the existing prices being offered by bottled-in-origin brands. This could lead to a shift in the competitive dynamics for other whiskies, including Indian single malts," said Sandeep Arora, founder of Spiritual Luxury Living according to the financial daily."Price differences, the entry of new whiskies, and availability will be key factors for the Indian market," he said.Before the lower prices could be introduced, the companies were required to submit proposals to state excise authorities and provide documentation establishing that the whiskies originated in the UK. People familiar with the matter said some states have already approved the proposed price reductions.Diageo had previously projected that prices across its bottled-in-origin Scotch portfolio could decline by around 7-9% on a nationally weighted average basis. The steeper reductions seen in some states are instead linked to differences in state-level pricing structures and individual commercial decisions, rather than being a direct reflection of the tariff cut.The lower prices could increase competitive pressure in India's premium whisky segment, including on Indian single malt brands such as Amrut, Paul John and Rampur. With imported Scotch becoming relatively cheaper, the price difference between the two categories is narrowing."While we have considered repricing to compete with these brands, we will have to wait till after the festive season to get a clearer picture of the market," said Rakshit Jagdale, company chief, Amrut Distilleries.The first round of price reductions is being introduced in some of India's largest whisky markets. Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh rank among the country's biggest whisky-consuming states, while Maharashtra and Haryana are important markets for Scotch.Pernod Ricard CEO Alexandre Ricard said in August that the company planned to use the agreement to make its brands "more relevant and more affordable to consumers", while also bringing new Scotch offerings to the market and speeding up innovation from Britain.
Article Summary: Scotch whisky prices in India have dropped by 10-15% for the first time since the India-UK free trade agreement came into force. Price cuts for brands such as Johnnie Walker Black Label and J&B have already taken effect in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Goa and Uttar Pradesh, while other states are expected to follow.

Article Title: No relook at bourses’ self-listing: Sebi
Article Text:
sebi chief tuh​in kanta pandey market statement

MUMBAI: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Wednesday said that there was no plan for the regulator to have a re-look at the current rule of not allowing self-listing of exchanges. He also said that the regulator was working with RBI to ease the onboarding process for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs).Pandey was speaking to journalists after addressing the annual conclave of the Association of Portfolio Managers in India. Regarding self-listing of bourses, the Sebi chief said that there was no proposal or plan to form a panel to consider such a move. Currently, when an exchange goes public, its shares are not traded on the same exchange’s trading platform. In India, BSE ’s shares cannot be listed and traded on BSE. Likewise, NSE ’s won’t be traded on NSE’s trading platform.Pandey insisted that the regulator cannot force foreign funds to invest in India, adding that Sebi is trying to ease the process for foreign funds to invest in the country. Sebi, meanwhile, is working with market players to finalise new CAS rules and it will stick to the recommendations in the recently published consultation paper on the process.During his speech, Pandey mentioned two recent and important developments for the PMS industry.Speaking about the recent Sebi board nod for reviewed Portfolio Managers Regulations, he said that one interesting addition was “the PRIM—the Portfolio Managers Route for Investing in Mutual Fund units.”“Under PRIM, portfolio managers can construct portfolios using direct plans of mutual funds, including ETFs, index funds and specialised investment funds,” he said. “This creates another space for professional portfolio construction. Instead of looking at investment products in separate silos, it allows a portfolio manager to use different pooled investment vehicles to build a portfolio around the needs of the client. ”The second interesting development was the introduction of the concept of Independent Fund Managers (IFM), the Sebi chief said. “This can create space for investment professionals and entrepreneurial talent to operate in association with an established portfolio manager. At the same time, accountability must remain clear. The registered portfolio manager will continue to bear responsibility for the activities of the Independent Fund Manager. ” The Sebi chief said that “opening up possibilities while keeping accountability clear runs through the new framework.”
Article Summary: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Wednesday said that there was no plan for the regulator to have a re-look at the current rule of not allowing self-listing of exchanges. He also said that the regulator was working with RBI to ease the onboarding process for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs)

Article Title: September pain on Dalal Street: FPIs pull out 46k crore from equities
Article Text:
Representational image

FPIs pull out 46k crore from equities

For the first time in two years, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) turned net sellers across all reported equity and debt segments in September.Also, on a standalone basis, FPIs were net sellers at Rs 35,861 crore in stocks till Sept 29. They net sold another Rs 10,148 crore worth of stocks on Sept 30, taking the month’s total figures to about Rs 46,000 crore, data from NSDL and BSE showed.The net selling figures for Sept in stocks came after two consecutive months of net buying: Rs 29,631 crore in Aug and Rs 20,200 crore in July. For the current year, net selling by FPIs at Rs 2.6 lakh crore is already way ahead of the previous year’s Rs 1.7 lakh crore net outflow by this influential investor group. The 2026 outflow is now the highest ever yearly net selling figure, NSDL data showed.Latest data showed that in addition to equities, FPIs were sellers in debt (general limit) at Rs 5,247 crore, in debt (VRR or Voluntary Retention Route) at Rs 5,049 crore, in debt (FAR or Fully Accessible Route) at Rs 10,431 crore and in hybrid at Rs 2,078 crore.FPIs were, however, net buyers in three of the five mutual fund segments: Rs 247 crore in equities, Rs 1 crore in debt and Rs 99 crore in hybrid, while they were net sellers in funds categorised under ‘other’ heads and didn’t put in any money in solutions-oriented schemes, NSDL data showed.The strong selling by FPIs in the current market came even as the rupee weakened, the price of crude oil—the single biggest import item for India—rose sharply to above the $115/barrel level for the Indian basket, and sensex and Nifty both lost about 6% each. While sensex lost 4,477 points to the month’s close at 72,480 points, Nifty lost 1,460 points to 22,620 points.
Article Summary: For the first time in two years, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) turned net sellers across all reported equity and debt segments in September. For the current year, net selling by FPIs at Rs 2.6 lakh crore is already way ahead of the previous year’s Rs 1.7 lakh crore net outflow by this influential investor group.

Article Title: Kotak Bank gets RBI nod to elevate ED Anup Kumar Saha to CEO post
Article Text:
Anup Kumar Saha

MUMBAI: RBI has approved Anup Kumar Saha’s appointment as managing director & CEO of Kotak Mahindra Bank for three years from Jan 1, 2027, with the bank’s board set to formalise the appointment and seek shareholders’ approval.Saha is currently whole-time director (executive director) at Kotak. He joined the bank in Jan 2026 and has overseen the retail bank, data analytics and marketing functions since March. Before joining Kotak, he held senior leadership roles at Bajaj Finance, culminating in his appointment as MD & CEO.C S Rajan, chairman, Kotak Mahindra Bank, said the bank looks forward to Saha's leadership in strengthening the franchise and in pursuing sustainable growth.Ashok Vaswani, managing director & CEO, Kotak Bank,who had announced his decision to step down after his term ends in December said Saha has experience across businesses, customer segments and operating functions. “Since joining Kotak, he has worked closely with our teams and demonstrated a clear understanding of the opportunities ahead,” he said.Saha said he was grateful to the board for the trust placed in him and looked forward to leading the bank.“I look forward to working with my colleagues to deepen customer relationships, tirelessly execute and build sustainable value for shareholders and all our stakeholders. We will remain firmly focused on doing the right thing and getting it right by the customer,” he said.Saha has over 32 years of professional experience, including 25 years in financial services across banking and non-banking financial institutions.During 14 years at ICICI Bank, Saha led businesses and functions spanning retail secured assets, business intelligence, retail and rural collections, credit cards and retail structured finance. Earlier, he worked with GE Capital across credit cards, sales and analytics and with Bharat Heavy Electricals in production engineering.Saha holds a BTech in engineering from IIT Kharagpur and an MBA from IIM Lucknow. As of June 30, 2026, Kotak Mahindra Group had 5,916 branches and a consolidated balance sheet of Rs 10.1 lakh crore.
Article Summary: RBI has approved Anup Kumar Saha’s appointment as managing director & CEO of Kotak Mahindra Bank. Saha is currently whole-time director (executive director) at Kotak. He joined the bank in Jan 2026 and has overseen the retail bank, data analytics and marketing functions since March.

Article Title: Inspiring story on marriage:“Our marriage is a partnership, we are equals who are figuring it out on the daily"- How Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce built a family rooted in love and partnership
Article Text:
Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce Image credit (Instagram)

Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce see marriage as a partnership

Kylie Kelce’s role goes far beyond the label of homemaker

Kelce

Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce put family before public expectations

The Kelces’ marriage shows why flexibility matters

Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce’s family-first approach

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce have built a marriage that often stands out for a simple reason: neither appears to treat family life as one person’s responsibility. Their approach came into sharper focus when Jason addressed criticism over Kylie’s role at home, explaining that their marriage works through shared effort rather than fixed expectations. Behind the NFL fame, packed schedules and public attention, the couple has created a family structure based on communication, flexibility and mutual support. Their story offers a relatable look at how two people can divide responsibilities while keeping the same goal at the centre: building a home together.Jason Kelce’s comments about his marriage came during a wider conversation about the role of homemakers and expectations placed on women. His response was notable because he did not describe Kylie’s contribution through a traditional label. Instead, he focused on the way the couple works together.“I don’t think of Kylie as a homemaker,” Jason replied, adding: “Our marriage is a partnership, we are equals who are figuring it out on the daily. The only expectation is that we love each other, support one another, and are committed to our family, that comes first.We both raise our kids, we both work, we both keep our home. It is both our faults it is messy, but such is life with 3 young children.”That explanation gives an insight into the way Jason views family responsibilities. The point was not that Kylie does not handle household duties. Instead, he described those duties as part of a wider arrangement that belongs to both partners.Their lives have also required flexibility. Jason spent years dealing with the demands of an NFL career, including travel, training, games and recovery. Kylie has taken on a major role in managing family life while also pursuing her own interests and work.Rather than presenting those responsibilities as permanent job descriptions, Jason described them as something the couple works out together.That distinction is important. A family’s needs can change. So can careers, schedules, finances and personal priorities. A partnership has to leave room for those changes.Kylie Kelce has often been associated with her role as a mother and wife, but her life includes much more than the work that happens inside the Kelce home.She has participated in community and advocacy work and has also developed her own public platform. Her identity is not limited to being Jason Kelce’s wife or the mother of their children.At home, however, raising children naturally requires a large amount of time and organisation. Child care, appointments, schedules, meals and everyday household decisions do not always appear in public, but they can shape the rhythm of family life.Jason has openly acknowledged his own involvement as a parent. In the documentary, one scene showed him caring for one of his young children while dealing with his own physical discomfort. The moment offered a more ordinary picture of life away from the football field.That kind of involvement matters because parenting is rarely about one dramatic gesture. It is built through repeated small tasks.Someone gets the child ready. Someone handles dinner. Someone manages an appointment. Someone stays awake when a child needs comfort. Sometimes the same person does more, and sometimes the balance shifts.For Jason and Kylie, the idea of partnership appears to come from recognising that both people contribute to the family, even when those contributions do not look identical.Being part of a famous family can create pressure to maintain a certain image. Jason and Kylie Kelce have instead spoken about family life in a way that feels grounded in everyday realities.Jason’s response to criticism showed that he does not believe a marriage should be defined by outsiders deciding what each partner ought to do. He described the couple as equals who continue to figure things out together.That approach also allows the family to adapt.Jason’s NFL career required a level of commitment that few ordinary jobs demand. His schedule could involve long days away from home and extensive travel during the season. Kylie therefore had to manage many aspects of family life around that reality.But an unequal amount of one type of work does not necessarily mean one partner has less value. A household involves many forms of labour, including financial support, child care, emotional support, planning and maintaining a home.The key issue is how couples decide to share those responsibilities.Jason and Kylie’s comments suggest that they do not see marriage as a competition over who contributes more. Instead, they appear to approach it as a shared project.That perspective can become particularly important when raising children. Their daughters are growing up in a household where both parents have demanding responsibilities, but where family remains the central priority.One of the most relatable parts of Jason’s comments was his admission that their home can be messy.“It is both our faults it is messy, but such is life with 3 young children.”The line may sound lighthearted, but it captures something many parents understand. Family life does not always look polished. A busy home with young children creates noise, clutter, rushed mornings and unexpected problems.The pressure to maintain a perfect household can make ordinary family challenges feel like failures. Jason’s comment offered a different perspective. A messy home can simply mean that people are busy living in it.That attitude also connects with the couple’s broader approach to responsibility. They appear to recognise that family life cannot always follow a fixed plan.A schedule that works one year may not work the next. A career change can alter the balance. Children grow and develop different needs. Personal goals can change too.A strong partnership therefore requires more than dividing tasks once and leaving them there. It requires regular conversations about what the family needs.For Jason and Kylie, that seems to be part of what keeps their relationship grounded.Their marriage has also developed in the public eye, where every comment can attract attention. Yet the principles Jason described are not particularly complicated. Love, support, commitment and shared responsibility form the foundation.Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce’s love story goes beyond being an NFL star and his wife balancing family life. Their relationship reflects how two people can build a family while managing demanding careers, parenthood and constant public attention.Jason’s comments shed light on how he views their partnership. He does not believe Kylie’s role in the family is defined by traditional gender expectations. Instead, he sees their responsibilities as part of an arrangement they have created together.That does not necessarily mean everything is split equally at all times. Family life can shift depending on circumstances, with one partner sometimes taking on more responsibilities while the other steps up when needed.For the Kelces, recognising each other’s efforts and respecting what each person brings to the family appears to be central to their relationship. Their approach suggests that partnership is less about dividing every task equally and more about supporting each other when circumstances change.Their marriage also highlights that equality does not require both partners to have identical roles. Different contributions can have equal value when both people appreciate the work involved and remain willing to share the responsibility.Away from the NFL, cameras and celebrity headlines, Jason and Kylie’s relationship reflects a more relatable side of family life. A strong marriage does not have to follow a perfect formula. It can simply involve communication, mutual respect and a willingness to figure things out together.For Jason and Kylie, building a family appears to be an ongoing process shaped by the needs of their lives and their shared commitment to making it work.
Article Summary: Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce have built a marriage that often stands out. Neither appears to treat family life as one person’s responsibility. Their marriage works through shared effort rather than fixed expectations. Their story offers a relatable look at how two people can divide responsibilities.

Article Title: Oil prices stay flat as markets weigh US-Iran talks and Middle East supply
Article Text:
Crude prices remain calm

Oil prices showed little movement in early trading on Thursday after both major benchmarks gained about $1 a barrel in the previous session. The oil market remained calm as investors weighed developments in US-Iran peace talks and the recovery in Middle East crude exports.Around 7 am IST, WTI Crude was trading at $90.16 a barrel, down 26 cents, or 0.29%, while Brent Crude stood at $97.93 a barrel, lower by 10 cents, or 0.10%.The largely flat session came after a strong September for oil prices. Brent has gained around 14% this month, marking its biggest monthly rise since July. WTI, meanwhile, has advanced about 5% over the month.Markets are also assessing the outlook for crude supplies from the Middle East as they track the latest developments around US-Iran peace talks. The movement in prices remained limited in early Thursday trading despite the gains recorded by both benchmarks in the previous session.The direction of WTI could depend on developments around the US-Iran negotiations. A new catalyst, such as progress in peace negotiations, will be needed for WTI to break below the immediate support level of $88 a barrel, he added.Qatar on Tuesday said that it hoped shuttle diplomacy between Tehran and Washington could result in a breakthrough.The comments came as uncertainty continued around the possibility of a deal between the two countries.US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, denied reports from Axios and CNN that cited US officials as saying he was prepared to offer Iran sanctions relief and release frozen Iranian funds in exchange for "concrete" steps from Tehran on its nuclear programme.The oil market is also tracking the pace at which supplies from the region are returning. Saudi Arabia resumed oil tanker loadings from Yanbu on Tuesday after restarting its East-West Pipeline.Gulf exports have also recovered, according to Goldman Sachs. The bank estimated that Gulf oil exports, including "dark exports" involving ships operating with their location transponders turned off, had reached 23.3 million barrels per day over the last week. That is in line with the 2025 average, while exports doubled in September, Goldman Sachs said in a note on Tuesday.Production policy is another factor in focus ahead of the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday. Two people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters that OPEC+ oil-producing countries are likely to leave their November oil production targets unchanged.US inventory data offered a mixed picture for the market. Crude stocks increased by 922,000 barrels to 427.3 million barrels in the week ended September 25, the Energy Information Administration said. At the same time, fuel inventories fell sharply, with the decline coming amid strong seasonal and global demand.
Article Summary: Oil prices showed little movement in early trading on Thursday. Both major benchmarks gained about $1 a barrel in the previous session. The oil market remained calm as investors weighed developments in US-Iran peace talks and the recovery in Middle East crude exports.

Article Title: Oil stays above $103 after Trump denies easing sanctions on Iran
Article Text:
Oil prices inch higher

Qatar seeks common ground

Middle East supply picks up

Oil prices inched higher on Wednesday, trading beyond the $103 per barrel mark as uncertainty over the US stance towards Iran returned to the spotlight. US The momentum came after US President Donald Trump rejected a report that Washington was prepared to ease sanctions on Tehran. Qatar, meanwhile, said it was continuing efforts to bring Iran and the US towards an agreement.Brent crude rose 0.56% to $103.20, while WTI crude gained 0.11% to $89.48. The gains came a day after oil prices declined as crude supplies from the Middle East showed signs of recovering.As the Strait of Hormuz remains choked for a seventh month, oil prices have continued to rise. Brent is set to gain around 14% in September, which would be its biggest monthly increase since July. WTI is headed for a rise of about 4% after crossing $106 for the first time since May.The gap between Brent and WTI has also widened to its highest level in four months this month. Traders have been assessing possible US restrictions on diesel exports, which could result in an oversupply in the domestic market and reduce the amount of crude processed by US refiners.Trump is considering allowing sales of red-dyed diesel instead of imposing an export ban, according to Reuters.The move would be aimed at offering some relief to consumers as the November mid-term elections approach.Qatar on Tuesday said that it hoped its shuttle diplomacy between Iran and the US could help the two sides reach a breakthrough."We are exchanging messages between the parties, and we're working towards establishing a common ground in order to get into a deal that would save all of us from the repercussions of the conflict," Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said.The diplomatic efforts came amid a report by Axios that cited US officials as saying Trump was willing to offer Iran sanctions relief and release frozen Iranian funds in return for "concrete" steps by Tehran on its nuclear programme.Trump rejected the report, saying "This is untrue. I offered them NOTHING."The recovery in regional oil flows has also emerged as a key factor for the market. Saudi Arabia resumed oil tanker loadings from its Red Sea port of Yanbu on Tuesday after restarting operations on the East-West Pipeline.Oil exports from Middle Eastern producers rose to 16.328 million barrels per day in September, their highest level since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in late February.US inventory figures also remained in focus. Crude oil and gasoline stocks increased last week, while distillate inventories declined, according to market sources citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.US crude inventories rose by 1.02 million barrels in the week ended September 25, the sources said.The official US Energy Information Administration inventory data is due at 10:30 a.m. EDT (1430 GMT). Analysts polled by Reuters expect crude and product inventories to have declined.
Article Summary: Brent crude rose 0.56% to $103.20, while WTI crude gained 0.11% to £89.48. The momentum came after US President Donald Trump rejected a report that Washington was prepared to ease sanctions on Tehran. Qatar said it was continuing efforts to bring Iran and the US towards an agreement.

Article Title: Nvidia announces record $150 billion share buyback amid AI boom
Article Text:
Nvidia’s growth outlook remains closely tied to the global AI infrastructure boom. (Reuters)

Nvidia has increased its share buyback authorisation by a record $150 billion, taking its total remaining repurchase capacity to $235 billion as the chipmaker bets on continued demand for artificial intelligence hardware amid intensifying competition.The increase surpasses Apple’s $110 billion buyback authorisation in 2024 and comes as investors question whether the massive spending on AI infrastructure that has driven Nvidia’s rapid growth can continue at its current pace.Shares of Nvidia, based in Santa Clara, California, rose more than 2%. The stock was up just over 20% this year through Friday, broadly in line with the Nasdaq 100 but well behind AMD, whose shares have more than doubled, and Intel, which has more than tripled.Nvidia said it expects to deploy the remaining $235 billion in buyback capacity through fiscal 2028. The company is generating billions of dollars in cash from strong demand for its processors, allowing it to increase shareholder returns while continuing to invest in its business.“The AI buildout won't continue at its current pace forever, but Nvidia is signaling confidence that demand for its hardware and services has staying power,” said Jacob Bourne, an analyst at Emarketer told Reuters.“Its cash generation is currently strong enough that it believes it can continue investing heavily in the business while also returning capital to shareholders,” he added.Nvidia shares were trading at about 16.5 times their 12-month forward earnings, their lowest multiple since January 2015 and below the 15-year average of 30, according to LSEG data. Some analysts see the lower valuation multiple as a sign that investors expect slower profit growth.Nvidia’s growth outlook remains closely tied to the global AI infrastructure boom. Last month, the company forecast about 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, reassuring investors who have questioned how long the AI spending surge can continue after years of rapid growth.“Our cash generation gives us the capacity to invest in the technologies that advance this transformation and return capital to shareholders,” CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement.The company ended the July quarter with $22.44 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Nvidia had last announced an $80 billion share buyback in May.The latest $150 billion increase in its buyback authorisation is larger than the market capitalisation of about 84% of S&P 500 companies, according to LSEG data. Nvidia’s latest buyback signals that the company remains confident in the durability of demand for its AI chips and services.
Article Summary: N Nvidia has increased its share buyback authorisation by a record $150 billion. The increase surpasses Apple’s $110 billion buybackAuthorisation in 2024. Nvidia said it expects to deploy the remaining $235 billion in buyback capacity through fiscal 2028.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Brent Crude rises for second session as US-Iran conflict fuels supply concerns
Article Text:
Oil prices rise for second day.

Oil prices

today:

Oil prices rose for a second consecutive session on Tuesday as concerns over potential disruptions to Middle East supplies due to the US-Iran conflict outweighed signs of recovering crude exports from the region.Brent crude futures rose $1.49, or 1.4%, to $106.77 a barrel by 8:56 am IST. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained $1.34, or 1.5%, to $93.94 a barrel. Both benchmarks had closed the previous session nearly $1 higher.At 7:30 am IST, Brent was up 63 cents, or 0.6%, at $105.91 a barrel, while WTI had risen 72 cents, or 0.8%, to $93.32.Crude exports from major Middle Eastern producers increased to 12.8 million barrels per day in September, the highest level since February, preliminary data from oil analytics firm Kpler showed on Monday.The increase was driven mainly by higher shipments from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.However, the recovery in exports has done little to ease concerns about the potential impact of the conflict on regional oil supplies, particularly through the Strait of Hormuz.US and Iranian officials separately held talks with mediators in a renewed effort to end the seven-month conflict, officials from both countries said.Further negotiations are widely expected to focus on an amended version of a seven-day proposal put forward by Iran last week on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.The conflict, which began in late February with US and Israeli attacks on Iran, has drawn renewed attention to the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route for global oil and gas supplies. Any disruption to the waterway could have a significant impact on energy markets.Meanwhile, the United States is considering regulatory relief to allow wider sales of red-dyed diesel as part of efforts to lower fuel prices, Reuters reported citing sources.The proposal could allow some buyers to avoid the federal fuel tax. It emerged after several days of deliberations as an alternative to a proposed ban on diesel exports.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures rose $1.49, or 1.4%, to $106.77 a barrel by 8:56 am IST. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 1.5% to $93.94 a barrel. Both benchmarks had closed the previous session nearly $1 higher.

Article Title: India's Essar Group to invest $15 billion in 'largest' US steel plant, Trump announces
Article Text:
President Donald Trump speaks as from right, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Energy Secretary Chris Wright, Essar Capital Director Prashant Ruia, Mesabi Metallics Chairman Rewant Ruia and Mesabi Metallics CEO Joe Broking

Project to link

Minnesota iron ore mine

with

Iowa steel plant

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday announced plans by Indian conglomerate Essar Group, through its US subsidiary Mesabi Metallics, to invest about $15 billion in a major steel plant in Iowa.Trump made the announcement at the White House alongside Essar Group co-founder Ravi Ruia and Mesabi Metallics chairman Rewant Ruia, describing the project as the largest steel plant in American history."Today we're thrilled to announce that Mesabi Metallics will be building the largest steel plant in American history in the great state of Iowa. It's the largest plant, one of the largest plants in the world, but it's the largest plant in America by far," Trump told reporters.The facility is expected to produce 10 million tonnes of steel a year once fully operational, with production targeted to begin in 2030. The project is also expected to create thousands of jobs during construction and nearly 2,000 permanent positions across the steel and mining operations.The Iowa plant will form part of an integrated US supply chain, with iron ore sourced from a new mine being developed by Mesabi Metallics in Minnesota's Mesabi Iron Range.The company has invested about $2.5 billion in the mine, which is expected to produce around 7.5 million tonnes of iron annually and create about 350 jobs.Rewant Ruia said he was born in India but had studied in New York, Boston and California, adding that he had spent half his life in the US and described the investment as "a true homecoming". He said the project would establish a fully integrated supply chain "from mine to mill".Trump highlighted the domestic nature of the operation, saying the Minnesota mine would be "the first new iron ore mine in the United States in more than 50 years with the highest quality ore.""In other words, this steel will be mined, melted, and made right here in the USA, which is something very unusual," Trump said.Rewant Ruia thanked the president "for bringing back the importance of building things in America." He also said the plant would use advanced technology and "will compete head-to-head with any steel plant in the world on size, quality and on cost."Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick attributed the investment partly to the administration's steel tariffs. Trump said companies were building in the US "because they don't want to pay tariffs".
Article Summary: Indian conglomerate Essar Group to invest about $15 billion in a major steel plant in Iowa. The facility is expected to produce 10 million tonnes of steel a year once fully operational, with production targeted to begin in 2030. The Iowa plant will form part of an integrated US supply chain, with iron ore sourced from a new mine in Minnesota.

Article Title: China cuts tariffs on US farm goods, but keeps soybeans on the other side
Article Text:
China cuts tariffs on US farm goods

China is offering Washington a little tariff relief — but the door is far from fully open.Beijing plans to cut tariffs on several US agricultural goods, while keeping an additional 10% tariff on soybeans, one of the biggest US farm exports to China.The Chinese commerce ministry’s tariff-reduction list issued on Monday includes corn, wheat, sorghum, vegetable oils and meals, meat and dairy products, among other agricultural goods. Soyoil and soymeal are also covered, while whole US soybeans have been excluded.The decision comes after last week’s summit in Washington between Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, with markets closely watching for details on tariff relief for US farm products.The treatment of soybeans stands out as Chinese state-run buyers continue to purchase the commodity from the US. Sinograin and COFCO have bought more than 12 million metric tons of US soybeans so far. That is nearly half of the 25 million metric tons that the White House has said China agreed to purchase each year through 2028.US soybeans will nevertheless continue to carry the additional 10% tariff. Traders have said this level remains too high for private crushers to absorb, although state buyers have stepped up their purchases."Despite the soybean being a non-sensitive item in trade, the political significance of China's soybean purchase is enormous and carries major political implications," said Feng Chucheng, founder and partner at Hutong Research."Hence a separate track on soybean purchase outside the Board of Trade. This also gives Beijing a leverage to restrain US actions, especially ahead of the midterm elections."The broader tariff reductions could help address the value of agricultural purchases that China has committed to making from the US. Trade in the agricultural and related products included in Monday’s list was worth about $17 billion in 2024, according to Reuters calculations. That is roughly equivalent to the reported purchase commitment when soybeans are excluded.The White House said in May that Beijing had agreed to buy $17 billion worth of these products annually through 2028. China has not, however, confirmed any target for such purchases.A trader based in Asia, who works for an international company selling soybeans to China and spoke on condition of anonymity, said state-run companies would continue purchasing US soybeans. The trader said the tariff reductions covering other products would help China meet the $17 billion commitment.However, the trader said lower tariffs would not necessarily make US soybeans competitive on price.The tariff moves are part of a wider effort by Beijing and Washington to maintain economic and trade ties. Both sides have agreed to set up a trade council, with its first task being discussions on a reciprocal tariff reduction covering $30 billion worth of products.While the new list covers a broad range of US agricultural goods, soybeans remain outside the tariff reduction, leaving purchases of the commodity to continue separately from the broader tariff-cutting measures.
Article Summary: Beijing plans to cut tariffs on several US agricultural goods, while keeping an additional 10% tariff on soybeans. Soyoil and soymeal are also covered, while whole US soybeans have been excluded. The treatment of soybeans stands out as Chinese state-run buyers continue to purchase the commodity from the US.

Article Title: US, China eye lower tariffs on $30 billion of goods each in fresh trade framework
Article Text:
Under the arrangement, US could gain better access to the Chinese market for agricultural products.

What the new trade arrangement covers

New mechanism to manage trade

Xi’s US visit

The United States and China have agreed to explore lower tariffs on selected goods worth about USD 30 billion each, as Washington and Beijing seek to ease trade tensions following Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to the US.Under the arrangement, US exporters could gain better access to the Chinese market for products including agricultural goods and medical devices. American consumers could also benefit from lower tariffs on selected Chinese imports such as household products, toys and other goods.US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced the recommendations late Sunday under a new Board of Trade created after US President Donald Trump’s visit to Beijing in May."As a direct result of the strong relationship between President Trump and President Xi, the United States and China, under the auspices of the new Board of Trade, have recommended USD 30 billion of trade in non-sensitive goods on each side that could benefit from more favourable tariff treatment in the future,” Greer said in a statement."From agricultural products to medical devices, President Trump is unlocking improved market access for about 30 per cent of US exports to China, while benefiting consumers with imports from China of household goods, toys, and other products that the United States generally does not import from other countries,” he said.The framework focuses on non-sensitive products that both countries agree could receive lower tariffs. Each side has proposed goods worth roughly USD 30 billion for consideration.The US list currently contains 77 tariff entries. They include plastic tableware, bed and table linen, umbrellas, kitchen appliances, playing cards, sports equipment and Christmas decorations.Any future tariff cuts will still have to go through the domestic legal procedures of both countries before they can take effect.The US Trade Representative said the Trump administration would continue pushing for what it described as fair, balanced and reciprocal trade with China. Washington also wants Beijing to meet its commitments on agricultural and energy purchases.The Board of Trade is intended to provide a regular channel for discussions over the selected products and their tariff treatment.Its US principals are treasury secretary Scott Bessent and Greer, while China is represented by Vice Premier He Lifeng.Deputies from both countries worked on the proposed product lists and will oversee trade involving the selected goods. They are expected to meet at least once every quarter and can recommend changes to the lists.However, the terms of reference say the two governments do not expect to make changes more than once a year.The announcement followed Xi’s three-day visit to the US, which began on Wednesday with Trump giving him a rare welcome at the aircraft.The two leaders held talks at the White House for more than two hours on Thursday before attending a state dinner hosted by Trump in Xi’s honour.A Chinese readout said the economic and trade teams had reached a new joint arrangement, describing it as positive for businesses and people in both countries as well as the wider global economy.The latest framework does not automatically reduce tariffs. Instead, it sets out a process through which Washington and Beijing can identify specific goods for potentially more favourable tariff treatment.
Article Summary: US could gain better access to the Chinese market for agricultural products. American consumers could also benefit from lower tariffs on selected Chinese imports. Announcement follows Xi’s three-day visit to the US, which began on Wednesday with Trump giving him a rare welcome at the aircraft.

Article Title: Seven months into Hormuz shutdown: Oil remains elevated as Trump rejects Iran proposal
Article Text:
Oil remains elevated as Trump rejects Iran proposal

Oil prices rose on Monday as Middle East tensions kept markets on edge after US President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s proposal to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. With this, oil markets have continued to remain volatile for seven months now, since US and Israel launched joint stirkes on Iran on Febraury 28.Brent crude climbed 1.18% to $105.50 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gained 0.77% to $93.12.The latest gains after Iran put forward a peace proposal at the United Nations General Assembly in New York last week. Tehran said the proposal had been conveyed to the US through Qatari mediators. However, the proposal was rejected by Trump on Saturday.The US President told Axios in a phone interview that he expected US negotiators to enter into further talks this week, leaving the possibility of renewed discussions open even as the proposed deal was rejected.Tensions in the region also remained elevated following a statement from Yemen's Saudi-led coalition. Early on Saturday, the coalition said it had intercepted two ballistic missiles and two drones launched towards Saudi Arabia by the Iran-backed Houthis.The latest gains in oil came after a mixed performance last week. Brent had edged 0.4% higher over the week, while WTI dropped 7.9% as concerns grew that the US could prohibit diesel exports to bring down record prices.A US restriction on diesel exports could also reduce refining output in the country. At the same time, it would tighten supplies in markets outside the US, with European prices responding to the prospect of lower American diesel availability.Despite the continued tensions, oil exports from major Middle East producers picked up in September. Preliminary Kpler data showed crude exports from key producers had risen to 12.8 million barrels per day, the highest level since the war began in February.Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates contributed to the increase by raising their exports. The recovery also reflected a rise in shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, with flows through the key waterway expected to reach about 7.4 million barrels per day this month.Saudi Arabia shifted exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu to Ras Tanura on its eastern coast after attacks damaged its East-West pipeline. The diversion contributed to the recovery in shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: Brent crude climbed 1.18% to $105.50 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gained 0.77% to £93.12. Latest gains after Iran put forward a peace proposal at the United Nations General Assembly in New York last week. Tehran said the proposal had been conveyed to the US through Qatari mediators.

Article Title: US diesel ban: Why cheaper diesel could come with a gasoline price shock
Article Text:
Why cheaper diesel could come with a gasoline price shock

What happens if diesel storage fills up?

Europe could see diesel prices rise

A possible US restriction on diesel exports could have a mixed impact on fuel prices. Diesel prices in the US could fall at first as more fuel stays in the country, but gasoline prices could later rise if refiners are forced to cut production, Goldman Sachs said.The bank said restrictions on diesel exports, including quotas, were a possible scenario, although it was not its base case. It modelled a possible ban starting in early October and lasting through at least December. A 90-day restriction is reportedly being considered.The impact would first be felt in the US diesel market. With exports restricted, more diesel would remain in the country, pushing up inventories. As long as there is enough storage space, this could put pressure on diesel prices.Goldman Sachs estimates that every week of an export ban could lower average US retail diesel prices by around $0.25 per gallon while storage space remains available.US diesel exports have already increased from 1.1 million barrels per day (mb/d) in 2025 to around 1.6 mb/d in recent months. At the same time, the national average retail diesel price has risen to $6.5 per gallon, according to the report.The fall in diesel prices may not continue if inventories keep rising and storage space becomes limited.Goldman Sachs estimates that US diesel inventories could theoretically fill up within 9-10 weeks if exports fell by 1.6 mb/d. However, the bank said this could take longer in practice because refiners could reduce production and demand for diesel could increase.Once storage becomes tight, the pressure could shift to refiners.Lower diesel prices could reduce refining margins and encourage refiners to cut output. This could also reduce the amount of gasoline and jet fuel produced.That could push US gasoline prices higher. Goldman Sachs estimates that once diesel storage is full, every additional week of an export ban could put around $0.30 per gallon of upward pressure on US retail gasoline prices.The bank also said gasoline prices could start facing upward pressure even before diesel storage reaches its theoretical limit, as refiners reduce production.The impact could also be felt outside the US.Goldman Sachs expects diesel prices in Europe and other markets to rise if US exports are restricted. It estimates that every week of an export ban could increase European wholesale diesel prices by around $3 per barrel, or just under 2%.However, releases from European strategic reserves could help limit the increase. Goldman Sachs estimates that these releases could offset around half of the rise.Meanwhile, the effects of a temporary export ban could continue even after restrictions are lifted.Goldman Sachs said US diesel prices would likely reconnect with international prices once the restrictions end.
